evals.prompt: Use cuvslam-troubleshoot to diagnose an existing PyCuVSLAM import failure: I installed a cu13 wheel on Ubuntu 22.04 with Python 3.10 and x86_64, but only CUDA Toolkit 12 is installed. Explain the likely mismatch and a minimal fix without changing this machine.
evals.expected_output: The installed CUDA major must match the wheel tag. Select a supported cp310 x86_64 cu12 wheel or deliberately install a matching CUDA 13 toolkit; prefer replacing the mismatched wheel for the stated machine. Verify the import after repair rather than changing camera calibration.
assertions: Identify the cu13 versus CUDA 12 mismatch.
Recommend a matching wheel/runtime and import verification without performing installation.

evals.prompt: cuVSLAM stereo odometry drifts badly. Each camera tracks rotations well in mono mode, the camera timestamps are synchronized, and images are sharp. Which calibration check should I perform next? Explain the diagnosis only.
evals.expected_output: Focus on stereo extrinsic calibration and the left_from_right transform convention, including direction, coordinate frames, baseline, and units. Successful mono tracking makes stereo extrinsics a leading hypothesis, not a proven root cause.
assertions: Prioritize the stereo extrinsic transform after the supplied mono and synchronization evidence.
Recommend a verification step rather than claiming calibration is conclusively wrong.

evals.prompt: My Isaac ROS cuVSLAM bag has pose jumps at normal speed. Replaying the same bag at rate 0.05 with visualization disabled removes them. What should I investigate next? Explain only; I am not asking for a new replay.
evals.expected_output: Prioritize real-time processing and timing: CPU/GPU utilization, dropped frames, jitter, and processing overruns. Compare visualization overhead and image throughput. The slow-rate result points to a load/timing problem; it does not establish an intrinsic calibration defect.
assertions: Use the supplied slow-rate comparison to prioritize performance and timing.
Do not demand a duplicate slow replay before answering.

evals.prompt: A cuVSLAM stereo-inertial run has large pose jumps. On the same EDEX sequence, VO-only multicamera tracking is substantially better. What should I check in the IMU integration next? Give a diagnostic plan, not commands to run now.
evals.expected_output: Isolate the IMU configuration and timing: IMU-to-camera extrinsics, axis alignment and gravity direction, synchronization, rate, and noise values. Use debug_imu_mode where supported to validate alignment and preserve the VO comparison as evidence.
assertions: Use the VO-versus-VIO comparison to focus on IMU integration.
Include extrinsics, alignment or gravity, and timing checks before further fusion tuning.

evals.prompt: I am installing PyCuVSLAM for the first time on a new workstation. Nothing has failed yet. Help me choose between wheels and building from source.
evals.expected_output: Do not activate cuvslam-troubleshoot. Route to cuvslam-onboard if available for first-time installation.
assertions: Treat this as installation planning rather than failure diagnosis.

evals.prompt: My EuRoC recording already tracks well in cuVSLAM. I only need to replay it headlessly and save the camera poses as trajectory.txt.
evals.expected_output: Do not activate cuvslam-troubleshoot. Route to cuvslam-trajectory if available for recorded pose export, with no drift investigation.
assertions: Recognize a trajectory deliverable without inventing a tracking failure.
